Title: UX-001 — SLA Pill in Task List Rows
Problem Statement: Agents and Managers cannot see SLA remaining time or SLA status in the task list — they must open each task individually to discover urgency. This causes missed SLAs and reactive rather than proactive triage.
Proposed Solution: Add an SLA status pill to every task card row in the list showing one of: "Inside SLA (Xh Xm)" / "Approaching SLA (Xm)" / "Overdue (by Xh Xm)". Use colour + icon + text label (never colour alone) with tokens: --color-success / --color-warning / --color-error. Update every 60 seconds via polling.
User Impact: High — enables self-prioritisation for agents; reduces Manager reassignment burden; prevents SLA breach by surfacing urgency at glance.

Title: UX-002 — Inline Character Counter on Comment Box
Problem Statement: The comment character limit (10–100 chars) is only discovered when validation fails on submit. Agents enter free text without knowing the range. This creates frustration and repeated re-entry friction.
Proposed Solution: Add a live character counter beneath the comment textarea that appears on first keypress. Format: "23/100 characters". Counter turns --color-error when count is < 10 (too short) or attempts to exceed 100 (truncate input at 100). Display hint text before typing: "Minimum 10, maximum 100 characters."
User Impact: High — eliminates the most common source of comment submission failure; reduces error recovery loops for agents.

Title: UX-003 — Allowed Characters Hint on Comment Box
Problem Statement: Users do not know which special characters are allowed in the comment field until they trigger a validation error. Allowed: letters, numbers, spaces, comma, period, hyphen, double-quote, forward-slash. Error discovery forces re-typing.
Proposed Solution: Show persistent hint below the comment box on focus: "Allowed characters: letters, numbers, spaces, , . - "/. Do not modify input silently — show inline warning immediately when an invalid character is typed and prevent it from being entered.
User Impact: High — prevents silent validation failure; reduces re-entry loop; aligns with error prevention heuristic.

Title: UX-004 — Dynamic Confirmation Modal Content
Problem Statement: The confirmation popup shows generic text regardless of the action type. Agents cannot distinguish between Complete and Cancel actions from modal text alone. Risk of accidental irreversible action.
Proposed Solution: Replace static confirmation text with dynamic content that mirrors the selected action: title ("Mark as Complete" / "Cancel Task" / "Reassign Task" / "Escalate Task" / "Reprioritise Task"), task ID + title in body, SLA continuation notice where applicable. Use green header for completion; red header for cancellation.
User Impact: High — prevents irreversible accidental actions; addresses error prevention (H5-03); builds user confidence.

Title: UX-005 — Structured Reason Picker for Cancel/Reject
Problem Statement: When cancelling or rejecting a task, agents enter free text with no guidance on valid reasons. This produces inconsistent audit records, non-searchable data, and no basis for reporting rejection patterns.
Proposed Solution: Replace free-text cancellation reason with a structured dropdown of pre-defined reasons (e.g., "Customer not available" / "Duplicate task" / "Out of jurisdiction" / "Customer cancelled request" / "Safety concern — cannot proceed" / "Other — see comment"). Always require a comment as well. Reasons configurable by Admin.
User Impact: Medium — improves audit quality; enables cancel reason analytics; reduces cognitive load for agents.

Title: UX-006 — Metric Tile Drill-Through on Dashboard
Problem Statement: Dashboard KPI tiles (Total / Inside SLA / Approaching SLA / Overdue) are display-only. Managers must manually re-apply filters to see the corresponding subset of tasks. This adds friction to the morning SLA review flow.
Proposed Solution: Make each metric tile a focusable button. On activation: automatically apply the corresponding filter to the task list panel below and scroll page to task list. Use aria-label: "View X Overdue tasks". Show active filter chip above list: "Filtered by: Overdue × [clear]".
User Impact: High — accelerates Manager triage workflow; reduces 3 steps to 1 action; high-value low-effort improvement.

Title: UX-007 — Business Area Switcher for Manager and Admin
Problem Statement: Managers and Admins currently have no mechanism to view tasks from a different Business Area. Interview confirmed this is a pain point for cross-area triage. Admin requires global visibility by role definition.
Proposed Solution: Add a Business Area Switcher in the dashboard toolbar. For Admin: dropdown shows all areas (default: All Areas). For Manager: shows own area (default) + read-only access to other areas. Persist selection in session. Show active area label as breadcrumb/header below page title.
User Impact: High — directly addresses interview pain point; enables cross-area awareness; prerequisite for Admin role fulfilment.

Title: UX-008 — SLA Reset Warning at Reprioritise Selection
Problem Statement: When an agent or manager selects "Reprioritise" from the action dropdown, there is no indication that this action resets the SLA timer until they read the confirmation modal. Many users will miss the implication.
Proposed Solution: Show a contextual callout immediately when "Reprioritise" is highlighted in the dropdown (before selection) and in the action panel after selection: "Warning: Changing priority resets the SLA timer. New SLA will be calculated from now." Also show calculated new deadline in confirmation modal.
User Impact: High — prevents unintended SLA manipulation; addresses H5-02 (error prevention); critical for SLA integrity.

Problem Statement: Dashboard KPI tiles and the task list are static after page load — SLA status changes (e.g.

User Impact: Poll the dashboard and task list every 60 seconds. Show: "Last updated: 1 min ago" beneath tiles. Animate newly changed rows subtly (colour fade) to draw attention. Allow manual refresh via a refresh icon button (aria-label: "Refresh task list"). Honour prefers-reduced-motion.
Effort (S/M/L/XL): High — prevents SLA breach from stale data; directly impacts Manager monitoring effectiveness.

Title: UX-010 — Agent Workload Count in User Picker
Problem Statement: When a Manager reassigns a task using the user picker, there is no indication of how many active tasks each agent currently has. Managers are reassigning blind, potentially overloading some agents while others are idle.
Proposed Solution: Display a workload count badge next to each agent name in the user picker: ""Ahmed (3 active)"" / ""Sanjay (1 active)"" / ""Ben (9 active — high)"". Colour-code: ≤ 4 = --color-success; 5–7 = --color-warning; 8+ = --color-error. Also show last-active timestamp.
User Impact: High — enables informed reassignment decisions; prevents over-assignment; reduces need for Manager chasing calls.

Title: UX-011 — Linear List with Accordion Cards as Default Layout
Problem Statement: User interviews confirmed that agents prefer a linear list layout over a grid. Current BRD does not specify layout type. Grid layout forces agents to scan across rows and columns and loses natural top-down priority reading order.
Proposed Solution: Default task list to vertical linear list with accordion cards. Collapsed state: Task ID + Title + SLA Pill + Status Badge + Priority label. Expanded on click: full detail including assignee + area + history + action panel. Remove grid toggle unless explicitly required by a user group.
User Impact: High — directly addresses confirmed user preference from interview; reduces scan time; improves mobile field app readiness.

Title: UX-012 — Reason-for-Change Gate on SLA Configuration
Problem Statement: Admin users can change SLA thresholds without providing a reason. Audit trail has entries but no rationale field. This creates a governance gap — changes cannot be reviewed for business justification.
Proposed Solution: Add a mandatory "Reason for change" text field in the SLA edit panel before Save is available. Minimum 10 characters. Reason stored in audit trail row alongside: changed-by user, timestamp, old value, new value, reason. Submit disabled until reason is entered.
User Impact: High — closes governance gap; provides audit trail that satisfies regulatory/compliance needs; Safe-by-Default change management.

Title: UX-013 — Export Audit Trail (CSV/PDF)
Problem Statement: Admin users need to present SLA configuration audit trails to business stakeholders and regulators. Currently, there is no export capability. Admins must screenshot or manually copy data.
Proposed Solution: Add Export button to the SLA Audit Trail panel with two format options: Download CSV and Download PDF. CSV exports raw data; PDF exports formatted report with company header. Filter the export by the same date range applied to the visible table.
User Impact: Medium — directly addresses Admin pain point from empathy map; enables compliance reporting; low technical complexity.

User Impact: On entering a new SLA value in edit panel: calculate and show live impact preview: "3 active tasks currently Inside SLA for Critical will become Overdue if you save this change." Use --color-warning background. Require acknowledgement checkbox before Save enables.

Title: UX-015 — Dismiss / Pause on Toast Notifications
Problem Statement: Non-urgent toast notifications (e.g., "Task saved successfully") auto-dismiss after 4 seconds. WCAG 2.2.1 requires users to be able to extend or pause time limits. Some users read slowly or use screen readers and miss the message.
Proposed Solution: Add a visible close (×) button on all toasts. Auto-dismiss timer: 8 seconds minimum for non-urgent (role=status). Pause timer on hover or keyboard focus. Critical/error toasts (role=alert) must not auto-dismiss — require explicit user dismissal.
User Impact: High — WCAG 2.2.1 compliance; screen reader users and slow readers cannot be forced to miss status messages.

Title: UX-016 — Task History Pinned in Detail Panel
Problem Statement: Task history (status change log) is not prominently visible in the Task Detail view. Agents and Managers must scroll to find it. When investigating a dispute or SLA breach, history is the primary reference source.
Proposed Solution: Pin a collapsed ""Task History"" accordion at the top of the Task Detail view immediately below the task header. Expand by default for Manager and Admin roles. Collapse by default for Agent role with count label: ""History: 4 events"".
User Impact: Medium — reduces investigation time for Manager/Admin; aids Agent context awareness; improves audit usability.

Title: UX-017 — Skip-to-Main Navigation Link
Problem Statement: All pages lack a skip-to-main content link. Keyboard-only users must tab through the full left navigation bar and header on every page load to reach the task list or main content area. This is a WCAG 2.4.1 Level A violation.
Proposed Solution: Add Skip to main content as the first focusable element in the DOM on every page. Visible only on :focus using position absolute pattern. Style with MET-DS-V2 focus token colours.
User Impact: Critical — WCAG 2.4.1 (Level A) violation; must fix before any release.

Title: UX-018 — Focus Trap in Modal Dialogs
Problem Statement: Modal dialogs (confirmation modal, user picker, critical task popup) do not trap keyboard focus. Tab key cycles out of the modal into the background page. This is a WCAG 2.1.2 violation and prevents keyboard-only users from completing modal interactions.
Proposed Solution: Implement focus trap using JavaScript on mount of each modal: detect first and last focusable elements; wrap Tab and Shift+Tab at boundaries. Move focus to modal heading or first CTA on open. Restore focus to trigger element on close.
User Impact: Critical — WCAG 2.1.2 (Level A) violation; keyboard users cannot complete any modal-based action.

Title: UX-019 — ARIA Roles on Interactive Components
Problem Statement: Several interactive components lack correct ARIA roles: status change dropdown does not announce selected value; notification toasts use plain <div> without role; filter chips do not use role="button" consistently.
Proposed Solution: Audit all interactive components: (1) <select> — use aria-describedby for action help text. (2) Toasts: role="alert" for errors/critical; role="status" for success. (3) Filter chips: role="button" with aria-pressed state. (4) User picker: role="listbox" with role="option" per item. (5) Metric tiles: role="button" if interactive.
User Impact: Critical — multiple WCAG 4.1.2 violations; screen reader users cannot operate system.

Problem Statement: Some status badges and SLA indicators rely on colour alone to convey meaning (red = overdue, amber = approaching SLA). Users with colour vision deficiency cannot distinguish statuses. This is a WCAG 1.4.1 Level A violation.

Title: UX-021 — SLA Business Hours Disclosure
Problem Statement: The SLA countdown timer calculates time within business hours (08:00–16:00), but this is not communicated in the UI. Users believe the SLA timer runs 24/7 and are confused when a task does not become overdue overnight.
Proposed Solution: Show inline note adjacent to every SLA countdown: ""SLA calculated within business hours: Mon–Fri 08:00–16:00."" Include this note in: Task Detail header

Priority (1=Critical): Medium — resolves a systemic mental model mismatch; reduces agent/manager confusion about SLA breach.

Title: UX-022 — Escalation vs Reassignment Explanation
Problem Statement: Users do not understand the difference between Escalate and Reassign without accessing documentation. Both actions involve directing a task to another user, but the business rules and consequences differ significantly.
Proposed Solution: Show inline description when each option is highlighted in the action dropdown: ""Reassign: Transfer task ownership within your Business Area. SLA continues."" / ""Escalate: Escalate to a senior user. SLA continues. Use for tasks requiring higher authority.""
User Impact: High — addresses a critical cognitive confusion that leads to wrong action selection; reduces misuse of escalation.

Title: UX-023 — Global Search Across All Areas
Problem Statement: Managers and Admins need to search for a specific task by ID or partial keyword across all business areas, not just the current view. Current search is scoped to the visible list only.
Proposed Solution: Implement a global search bar in the top navigation header. Search accepts task ID exact match (TASK-XXXXX) or keyword. Results show top 5 fast-match suggestions in a dropdown. Manager results scoped to own area; Admin results cross-area. Screen reader: announce result count on open.
User Impact: Medium — directly requested by Manager and Admin personas; enables quick navigation to any task.

Title: UX-024 — Field App Critical Task Acknowledgement
Problem Statement: The Field App (lightweight mobile surface) pushes a notification for Critical tasks. There is currently no acknowledgement mechanism — the agent cannot confirm they have received and seen the critical alert, and the Manager has no visibility.
Proposed Solution: Add an Acknowledge button to the Critical Task push notification on the Field App. On acknowledgement: (1) Update task history: ""Critical alert acknowledged by [agent name] at [time]"". (2) Notify Manager via dashboard feed. (3) If not acknowledged within 10 minutes: auto-escalate.
User Impact: High — closes the SLA safety loop between push notification and Manager awareness; reduces missed criticals.

Title: UX-025 — Reprioritise SLA Duration Preview
Problem Statement: When an agent or manager reprioritises a task to a higher or lower priority, they cannot see what the new SLA deadline will be until after they confirm. This makes it impossible to make an informed reprioritisation decision.
Proposed Solution: Show calculated new SLA deadline immediately in the action panel when a new priority level is selected: "New SLA deadline: Today 15:45 (4h from now at High priority)". Confirm the same information in the confirmation modal body before the user submits.
User Impact: High — enables informed priority decisions; prevents unintended SLA manipulation; supports H1 (system status visibility).
